items.rule: Names the metric in a short scan label.
Defines dashboard grouping and drill-in affordance.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, loading, risk, selected, focus, hover, default
items: Expose label, value, and delta as text.
Do not rely on sparkline or color alone for trend.
Use button or link semantics when the tile drills in.
Keep numeral and delta order logical for screen readers.
Risk tone must include visible threshold copy.

variants.copy: KPI Tile variants describe local metric anatomy. Dashboard groups, formulas, chart pairings, and drill-down ownership are pattern concerns.

states.copy: KPI Tile states communicate default, hover, selected, loading, risk, and disabled conditions without changing metric semantics.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant defines metric content; state defines interaction and threshold feedback.

full-width.copy: KPI Tile can fill a dashboard grid column; the grid owns column count and rhythm.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Use fewer columns on smaller viewports; never miniaturize values to force more tiles.

viewport-organization.copy: KPI Tile is a dashboard unit; layout decides how many tiles can fit without shrinking values.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Stack tiles and keep numerals readable.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Use two columns only when values stay readable.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use dashboard grid with controlled tile count.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify label, value, delta, tone, and sparkline behavior.
playground.snippet: <KpiTile label="Fuel spend" value="$84.2k" delta="+12% vs last week" trend="up" />

api-foundations.copy: KPI Tile API exposes metric content and state while Design System owns numeral role, tone, surface, and responsive density.

props.name: state
props.type: default | hover | focus | selected | loading | risk | disabled

props.name: ariaLabel
props.notes: Accessible name override for interactive tiles.

props.name: onSelect
props.notes: Local selection callback for button-style drill-in.

groups.title: Use
items: Use one clear metric per tile.
Use tone only for status or threshold.
Use sparkline only as secondary trend support.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not use KPI Tile as a generic card.
Do not hide risk in color only.
Do not put dashboard formulas or chart groups inside the component.

groups.title: Escalate
items: Metric groups, donut pairings, shared filters, and drill-down rules become dashboard patterns.

rejectIf: Sparkline is the only trend signal.
Dashboard composition is hidden inside KPI Tile.

miel.copy: MIEL treats KPI Tile as metric evidence: agents may propose it for one value, but humans confirm metric definition, owner, threshold, and drill-in.
canDecide: Use KPI Tile for one dashboard metric.
Use warning or danger only when threshold meaning is known.
Use sparkline only as secondary trend support.
mustAsk: Metric formula or data source is unknown.
Tile drill-in changes navigation or permissions.
rejectIf: The tile contains multiple unrelated metrics.
miel.handoff: I am using KPI Tile for a dashboard metric. Please confirm formula, threshold, owner, drill-in destination, and whether trend is required.

operational-example.copy: Use KPI Tile to summarize one operational metric with value, trend, threshold, and optional local drill-in affordance.

scenario.title: Fleet dashboard metrics
rationale: KPI Tile gives dashboards a repeatable metric contract before chart or table detail.
Numerals use Voice roles instead of arbitrary display sizing.
Tone is reserved for threshold meaning, not decoration.
